observations: Photo 0: a black widescreen LCD monitor, roughly 19 to 20 inch, on its round stand, screen switched off.
Photo 0: 'LG' logo on the lower bezel and 'FLATRON' with a small unreadable model code on the upper left bezel.
Photo 0: front panel buttons on the lower right bezel, no power light visible.
Photo 0: heavy dust on the screen and the stand base.
Photo 0: a black full size wired-style keyboard in front, worn and dusty, no brand legible.
Photo 0: no cables, no power adapter, no screen-on shot, no back panel or rating label shown.
Seller's own title calls the lot 'scrap', which conflicts with 'like new' and 'works perfectly'.

identity.kind: 19 inch LCD computer monitor with keyboard

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows an LG monitor and a keyboard in dusty, used condition, consistent with a scrap lot.
Photo 0 shows thick dust on screen and stand and a worn keyboard; the seller's own title says scrap.
No back panel or screw shots; opening cannot be confirmed from photos.
Screen is off in photo 0; no powered-on shot or clip.
No receipt or warranty document shown; for a monitor of this age a live warranty is unlikely.

risks.risk: Monitor does not power on or shows a dead or damaged panel (lines, dead pixels, backlight failure).
risks.proof: Short clip of the monitor powering on and showing a full white and a full colour screen, with the plug and power light in frame.

risks.risk: Power adapter or power cable and video cable missing.
risks.proof: Photo of all cables and the adapter laid out next to the monitor.
risks.if_unproven: as monitor without cables or adapter

risks.risk: Exact model and screen size unknown, which shifts the value band.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the rating label on the back of the monitor.
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest common Flatron size, about 18.5 inch

risks.risk: Keyboard keys dead or missing connector.
risks.proof: Clip of the keyboard typing into a text field on a connected computer.

risks.risk: Cracked or scratched screen hidden under dust.
risks.proof: Photo of the screen wiped clean and lit, at an angle.

proof_requests: Clip of the monitor powering on and showing a full white screen, power light in frame.
Photo of the rating label on the back of the monitor showing model and size.
Photo of the power adapter and video cable.
Clip of the keyboard typing on a connected computer.
Photo of the receipt and warranty card if they truly exist.
response.reason: An LG Flatron monitor and a keyboard are clearly shown, so the lot can be priced at its worst case as not working scrap; 'like new' is contradicted by the dust and the seller's own word 'scrap', and working condition, model and accessories need proof to raise it.
